subject: NX Logistics RFP — commercial proposal and usage-floor / credit-swap options
content:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@nxcorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commercial section clarifications — RFP NX-78

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the technical clarifications in the runbook. Procurement asked me to follow up specifically on the commercial/pricing section — they want a concise restatement of what you can commit to vs. optional credits/overage mechanics. A few specific asks:

- Provide an explicit mapping of commit tiers -> effective $/1k tokens and any associated minimums.
- Describe how overages are billed and if we can cap per-month overage spend.
- Explain the “usage-floor” and “credit-swap” language you referenced on the call; concrete examples would be helpful.
- Do you support quarterly true-ups vs. monthly?
- Attach any sample invoice(s) or a simple calculator we can run against our forecast.

Procurement would like this back by EOD PT so they can include it in their scoring.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Senior Sourcing Manager — Nexus Logistics
emily.zhang@nxcorp.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@nxcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:03:21 -0700
Subject: RE: Commercial section clarifications — RFP NX-78

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Below is a compact commercial response you can drop into the RFP commercial appendix; I also attached a one-page pricing card and an interactive calc (see attachments) with worked examples based on the forecast you shared on the call.

Executive summary (short):
- We offer committed monthly token volumes (commits) at stepped price bands. Commits buy a materially lower $/1k-token rate and include a guaranteed priority capacity SLA (reserved pool).
- Overages are billed at a higher rate but can be softened via an optional monthly "usage-floor" and a one-time "credit-swap" conversion that converts unused committed tokens into credits that can offset overage line items.
- True-ups: default monthly true-ups, optional quarterly true-up cadence for enterprise contracts.

Pricing mechanics (concise):
- Commit tiers (examples):
  * Tier A: 50M tokens/month -> $20 / 1k tokens (effective)
  * Tier B: 150M tokens/month -> $16 / 1k tokens
  * Tier C: 500M tokens/month -> $12 / 1k tokens
  (Exact tiers and rates are negotiable in contract; above are illustrative for NX forecasts.)

- Overages: billed at 2.5x the committed $/1k rate for the tier in which the usage occurs. Overages are measured at the monthly billing cycle and appear on the next invoice.
  * Example: Tier B committed rate $16/1k -> overage rate = $40/1k.

Usage-floor (optional add-on):
- Purpose: provide a soft cap on monthly bill volatility and allow NX to budget predictable worst-case spend.
- Mechanics: customer pays a modest monthly floor fee (e.g., 10% of commit value) that entitles them to a lowered overage multiplier for that billing period (e.g., 1.75x instead of 2.5x). The floor is independent of consumed volume and is refundable as credits at annual true-up if unused.
- Example: If NX purchases Tier B and opts into a 10% usage-floor, overage multiplier drops to 1.75x -> $28/1k instead of $40/1k.

Credit-swap (optional, one-time at contract start or renewal):
- Purpose: convert a portion of unused committed capacity into a flexible credit pool that offsets future overages or burst usage across months. Helps teams that have seasonal spikes.
- Mechanics: at the end of a quarter (or at renewal), up to X% of unused committed tokens can be converted to monetary credits at a negotiated swap rate (typ. 60–85% of the committed $/token value). Credits are usable for overages, premium model surcharges, or pro-feature seat licenses; they expire 12 months after issuance unless otherwise stated.
- Example: $100k worth of unused commit converts to $70k of credit (swap rate 70%) to be used against future overage charges.

True-up cadence and billing:
- Default: monthly measurement + invoice; 30-day invoice terms.
- Option: quarterly true-up (preferred for companies with bursty monthly volatility); we can align invoicing to quarter if NX prefers.

Misc commercial terms (high-level):
- Pilot: 3-month pilot at a reduced commit level (e.g., 25% of target Tier A volume) with a one-time pilot discount on commit pricing. Pilot volume can be folded into the committed baseline at renewal without penalty.
- Early termination: standard termination fees apply during committed terms; we can provide a pro-rated credit schedule on request.
- Cap on monthly overage spend: we can add an explicit hard cap as an SLA adjunct (requires minimum commit increase or an additional risk premium).

Attached: pricing_card_v2.pdf (one-page summary), redwood-pricing-calc-20261007.xlsx (workbook — inputs: forecast months, tier selection -> outputs: monthly invoice, cumulative cost, credit balances). Sample invoice template included in the workbook and a separate PDF.

Please see the attached calculator for two NX-specific scenarios I modeled: (A) steady-state 120M/mo; (B) seasonal peak with 3x spikes in Q4. I highlighted the net invoice delta between monthly true-up vs. quarterly true-up to show smoothing impact.

If procurement wants a written concession: we can offer a limited 10% sign-up credit applied to committed spend for contracts signed before the end of the pilot window. That credit cannot be used for overage charges and will appear as a line-item credit on the first invoice.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call with you + procurement to walk through the calc — I can share the workbook live and run a scenario.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Commercial — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
(Attachment: pricing_card_v2.pdf (PDF, 324KB))
(Attachment: redwood-pricing-calc-20261007.xlsx (Excel, 58KB))

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@nxcorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nxcorp.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 14:20:09 -0700
Subject: RE: Commercial section clarifications — RFP NX-78

Aditya — this is helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from Procurement:

- The overage multiplier at 2.5x is higher than some other vendors; can you bring that down to 2.0x if we take a 12-month commit and add the usage-floor?
- Procurement needs to see a sample invoice and a redlined SOW showing how the usage-floor and credit-swap will be represented. Can you attach a sample invoice (with values populated) and the standard SOW template?
- For the credit-swap, procurement prefers a minimum swap rate of 75% for credits that are usable against overages (and a 24-month expiry). Is there flexibility?

They also flagged billing frequency: quarterly true-up is preferable.

If you can return a short answer to those three points + updated sample invoice by EOD PT, Procurement will include Redwood in the final commercial evaluation.

Best,
Emily

------------------------------------------------------------------------
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@nxcorp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@nxcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 16:45:12 -0700
Subject: RE: Commercial section clarifications — RFP NX-78

Emily / Procurement — quick answers and concessions below; Laura and Rishi are looped for legal/finance sign-off on final wording.

1) Overage multiplier: we can reduce to 2.0x on a 12-month committed term if NX opts into the usage-floor (10% floor suggested) and agrees to quarterly true-up. This concession assumes the commit is >= Tier B in the example bands or a similarly sized commit (we can word it as a threshold).

2) Sample invoice & SOW: attached sample-invoice-202610.pdf (populated values for scenario A) and a draft SOW excerpt that shows how usage-floor fees and credit-swap appear. If procurement wants the full redline, Laura will coordinate with your legal team (cc’d).

3) Credit-swap rate & expiry: we can accept a 75% swap rate for credits usable against overages, and extend credit expiry to 24 months for this agreement, subject to a maximum convertibility cap of 30% of total committed value per contract year.

Next steps:
- I'll drop the updated sample invoice and SOW redline into the shared Drive link (https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-pricing) and ping legal.
- If procurement agrees to the 12-month commit + usage-floor + quarterly true-up, we'll issue a draft commercial amendment reflecting the reduced overage multiplier.
- We propose a short 30-minute call tomorrow to confirm acceptance and run one final invoice scenario live from the workbook.

Thanks — happy to finalize quickly.

Aditya Rao
Head of Commercial — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
(Attachment: sample-invoice-202610.pdf (PDF, 48KB))

---
Note: internal reviewers — Laura/Rishi, if you’re okay with the concession language I’ll draft the amendment and send to Kate at Nexus legal. If you want the concession to be conditional on an annual commit uplift, say so and I’ll include a clause.
